posts.cooked:
Vengeance game: Ermine, Proletariat, Fright Train and Friction head to Silver Gulch and find Chrono-Ranger, Sky-Scraper, Tempest and Omnitron-X.

Proletariat gets both his problem cards out early, but there's plenty of area effect damage and ongoing destruction on the hero's side so you can manage it. Also the environment is fairly helpful.

Mint, but everyone on around 7 hp. Hit hard, hit often and you'll be fine.

posts.name: Reverend Pete
posts.cooked:
Near Mint.

 

First game, I made two critical errors:

1. I used Micro Assembler on Omnitron X, forgetting that you need to discard a card as a part of its power. I had Defensive Blast in my hand and a plating out, so my intent was to fish for another plating, thinking "WOW, once I get this set up, the game will be a cakewalk! I'll show them how a robot rampages!" and then, since Defensive Blast was the *only* card in my hand at that point, I had to discard it, and Omniton X hung his head and cried cyber-tears of shame and sorrow.

 

2. I left Ermine for last. Why?  Uh...dunno. Lapse of Judgment? Flight of Fancy? Not paying attention? I thought--"Eh, I can ride it out."  Nope. Bad idea. Sky-Scraper went down at some point, but I had CR, Tempest and O-X in mid-single digits with only Ermine left. She soon produced 2 Subtle Diversions simultaneously, and I had no way to get rid of them. I watched all the HP slowly go away while I frantically tried to draw some ongoing destruction (which this team has plenty of...I had just squandered it early and wasn't drawing any more).

 

So Ermine stood victorious with about 5HP left.  

 

Second game went MUCH better. I took out Ermine relatively early, and had almost no problems. Sheriff Pratt ended the game by shooting Proletariat while boosted with 2 Aggression Modulators. That lawman was MAD!

posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
Powerhound_2000:

My guess is because overall her threat isn't taking out the heroes by damage but moreso screwing up any setup.  

With the exception of Iron Legacy, it seems to me that screwing up set-up is what makes a villain difficult, not ability to do damage.

I mean, look at the higher rated villains – Citizen Dawn's "avoid at all costs" card is Devastating Aurora, which does no damage. Gloomweaver was downgraded from a 3 to a 1, and I'm pretty sure the fact he has no forced ongoing/equipment destruction has a lot to do with that. While Voss is still rated at 3, I tend to find him consistently easy, because his deck has one card that does any Ongoing destruction, and it's a unique target with no in-built way to come back.

And of the lower-tier villains, the worst cards to face are the Flechettes and Devious Disruption because they wipe your board.

By this point in the game, there are tons of healing or DR options for most of the heroes, making damage itself less of a threat, while the real danger is losing the cards and combos you've spent the whole game setting up.

posts.name: bolnerap
posts.cooked:
Easy Mint with 11/8/8/13 HP remaining. All four enemies went down in my third round.

Tempest was far and away the MVP. Gene-Bound Shackles is total shenanigans in Vengeance as it is against the Ennead. Proletariat got out two extra clones and it didn't matter- between Silver Gulch, Sky Scraper, and Tempest's dueling "2 damage to everything" parties, he was wildly ineffective. In particular, Tempest round 2 was bonkers: 6/6/2 out of Chain Lightning, then 2 to everyone. By the time it came around to his third turn, Fright Train was down and everyone else was at 4 or less, making them easy pickings.

Hopefully I don't have to redo it - I see the latest iOS update is screwy - but I won't mess with anything until it gets fixed, and hopefully my one-shot collection is unaffected.
